basic_info.name: Concrete Crack Images for Classification
basic_info.description: Classification packaging of Concrete Crack Images for Classification with image-level labels for cracked and non-cracked concrete surfaces.

imaging_setup.lighting_conditions: Concrete building walls and floors with varied surface finishes (exposed concrete, plaster, paint) and illumination conditions

classes.name: non-cracked
classes.description: Concrete surface patch without visible crack

geographic_coverage.temporal_scope: Published 2018 (Mendeley Data v1, 2018-01-15; v2, 2019-07-23); collected at METU Campus, Ankara, Turkey

quality_assurance.annotation_quality: Image-level binary labels (20,000 Positive / cracked and 20,000 Negative / non-cracked 227x227 RGB patches) extracted from 458 full-resolution (4032x3024) photographs of concrete walls and floors at METU Campus following the patch-extraction procedure of Zhang et al. (2016) without random rotation or flipping augmentation (the ISARC 2018 paper rounds these figures to 500 source images and 224x224 patches). The source deposit provides no fixed train/val/test split folders (the companion paper uses a random 70/15/15 split). Across the 40,000 files there are 38,402 unique SHA-256 hashes (288 duplicate groups / 316 extra files in cracked, 1,231 duplicate groups / 1,282 extra files in non-cracked, and 0 cross-class duplicates).
